WHATSAPP.source: developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing (read 2026-10-24): user-initiated calls are free in every country; Meta bills the customer's own WABA directly, nothing goes through us.

providersWithoutRates.VOICELINK: No published rate: each account's plan sets its own inbound_rate, outbound_rate and pulse_seconds (app.voicelink.co.in/documentation/plans and the API context file, read 2026-10-21). The engine takes each call's own charge from GET /api/v1/call-log/details (total_cost, rupees) instead.

pipeline.note: What the engine bills each part of a PIPELINE stack on (costs.pipeline_cost), by model. stt: the whole call's minutes (the stream is open from start to end); llm: tokens in and out (thinking counts as out); tts: characters sent, or minutes of audio made for the token-billed ones (Gemini about 1,500 audio tokens a minute, 25 a second).

estimate.source: backend/voice/research/gemini-cost-2026-10-17.md, without session rotation (off since 2026-10-24): a booking agent (about 1,200 prompt tokens a turn, engine sections included) costs about $0.066 a talk-minute and a 5,479-token prompt $0.098 (Rs 6.1-6.4 and 9.2-9.4). Fitted to those two: $0.057 a minute plus $0.0000075 per prompt token; the $0.057 is the talk time (1,500 audio tokens a minute each way) and the conversation so far, which Gemini Live re-reads every turn. That part grows with the call: a 10-minute booking call comes to about Rs 19 a minute.
estimate.perMinuteSource: How a list price becomes a price per call-minute (usdPerMinuteOf in frontend/helpers/voice-stack.ts): a text model reads llmTokensPerTurn and writes llmOutTokensPerTurn, turnsPerMinute times; a voice says ttsCharsPerMinute characters, or a minute of audio; audio billed by the token runs at audioTokensPerMinute (Gemini 25 a second; OpenAI Transcribe's $0.003/min at $1.25/M is 2,400; OpenAI Realtime 1 token per 100 ms heard, per 50 ms spoken). A realtime model hears and speaks a minute of audio each.

tools.source: backend/voice/tools.py: the booking functions' declarations plus their '# Your tools' lines are about 2,100 characters; a custom tool sends its description twice (declaration and prompt) plus its parameters. A use reads the tool's answer as text.

stack.note: The models each part offers when the catalogue cannot be read, and the only list for Deepgram, Cartesia and ElevenLabs (no API gives their prices). Gemini and OpenAI models and prices come from the Vercel AI Gateway catalogue (frontend/server/voice-agent/voice-catalogue.ts). Each one's price is `pipeline` (realtime: `gemini`); first = default.
